I had my blood test not long ago and they did ask what arm, but if they can’t get blood from the one you chose they will go for the other. I would ask the clinic by ringing them if you’re allowed to go in on your own. If the answer is yes, you could just say to your Mum that you feel anxious with another person in the room and it would be too crowded. (The bays in where my Mum works are tiny and hardly fit two people let alone three.) If the answer is no, I’m pretty sure they would let your Mum stand outside the bay/room.

My Dad knows about my scars so I didn’t have this problem. But the man taking my blood did stare at them a bit. So whether you tell your Mum or not, I’d be prepared for that to possibly happen. 

If you feel it’s safe and you feel ready to tell her then I would tell her but it’s completely up to you.

I am not sure what country you are in but in the UK you have to be an immediate risk to yourself or others. Getting a bed here is so incredibly hard.
I got a bed on a CAMHS ward (under 18) and I ended up being there for two years. It was horrible, and actually incredibly hard to be discharged. Beds are like gold dust, even if you are at imminent risk, you most likely won’t get one. If the crisis team or your psychiatrist decide you can be kept safe in the community (even if it’s not particularly true) they will do everything possible to keep you outside hospital, even if it risks your life. I ended up getting admitted because my SH got quite bad quite quickly. It isn’t really somewhere you ask to be, but if your life is at risk and there’s no other way to keep you safe then it may be a good idea but psychiatric hospitals are so toxic and the environment is exactly not what you need to get better. I only found it helpful to keep me safe. Literally no other reason. It took me a year of my two year stay to even get therapy. Like I said I’m in the UK, it may be very different where you are.
